title: Peace & Conflict: Stretch
welcome_lead: Evaluate the hardest issues: nuclear weapons, terrorism, conscientious objection and modern conflict.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Peace & Conflict stretch — nuclear weapons, terrorism, conscientious objection.
final_note: You can now construct evaluative arguments on modern conflict for top marks.

concepts.def: Weapons of mass destruction — nuclear, chemical, biological
Nuclear weapons held to discourage attack
Violence on civilians to force political change
Person who refuses military service on moral grounds

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1945 the US dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, killing over 100,000 civilians.

The Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) was opened in 1968. Pope Francis (2019) called even possession of nuclear weapons immoral.

Many Christians argue WMD breaks 'discrimination' in Just War — civilians can't be spared.

Terrorism — deliberate violence on civilians — is condemned by mainstream Christianity and Islam.

Qur'an 5:32: 'Whoever kills a soul. it is as if he had slain mankind entirely.'

Muslim scholars worldwide signed the Amman Message (2004-2005) rejecting terrorism in Islam's name. Christian leaders (e.g. Archbishop of Canterbury) consistently condemn it.

A conscientious objector refuses to fight for moral/religious reasons.

In WW1 around 16,000 British men refused military service. Many Quakers served as stretcher-bearers or in the Friends Ambulance Unit.

Evaluate: pacifism preserves Jesus' teaching; Just War defends the innocent. A strong answer balances both views before reaching a conclusion.

Hinduism is straightforwardly polytheistic with millions of separate gods.
Hinduism worships no gods, only ancestors.
It is more accurately described as henotheistic or monistic — many gods (devas) are considered aspects or manifestations of one ultimate reality (Brahman).
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.

mcqs.q: What does the Buddhist doctrine of anatta teach?
options: Anatta means Buddhists have no personality.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
Buddhists believe in a soul like the Christian or Hindu version.
There is no permanent, unchanging self or soul — what we call 'self' is a constantly changing flow of five aggregates (skandhas). This is distinctively Buddhist and differs from the Hindu atman.

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
Hinduism worships no gods, only ancestors.
